transcript.text:
A dryer can legitimately continue for a cool-down or anti-crease phase, and an automatic programme can run longer if it still senses moisture. But if it keeps tumbling indefinitely after the programme has reached the end, that points more towards the moisture-sensing system or the timer/control. 1. If it will not respond to the Stop/Off button, switch it off at the wall and unplug it before doing anything else. Do not leave it running unattended.
2. Empty and clean the fluff filter, then wipe any metal moisture-sensor strips just inside the drum with a soft cloth lightly dampened with white vinegar; dry them afterwards. A coating from fabric softener can make a sensor programme run on.
3. Try a short timed programme, rather than an automatic/sensor one. If timed drying ends normally but sensor drying does not, the sensor or its cleanliness is the likely issue. If both run past the end, the programme control is more suspect. Does it keep tumbling after the display/timer reaches the end, or is it an automatic/sensor programme that keeps adding time before the end?
it shows End then the drum turns a bit every couple of minutes. stops if i open the door

That sounds like the normal anti-crease phase, rather than the dryer failing to stop. Many dryers show “End” but briefly turn the drum every few minutes to prevent clothes creasing; opening the door stops it, as it should. 1. Look for an anti-crease/crease-care option or symbol in the programme settings. Turn it off for the next load if you want the dryer to remain completely still once it reaches End.
2. If the drum only turns briefly at intervals and stops when the door opens, it is normally safe behaviour. It would be a fault if it starts running continuously again after showing End, becomes hot, or keeps doing this for an unusually long time with no anti-crease option selected. In that case, switch it off at the wall and an engineer may need to assess the control system.
whats anti crease? it goes on for about an hour if i leave it. worried its wasting electricity

Anti-crease is a clothes-care setting: after drying has finished, the dryer briefly tumbles the load at intervals so garments do not sit in one position and become heavily creased. An hour of occasional short turns can be normal on some dryers, and it should use far less electricity than active drying because the heater should be off once it shows End. It is not usually something to worry about if it only turns briefly every few minutes and stops when the door is opened. You can simply open the door and remove the clothes when it reaches End, or switch off any anti-crease/crease-care option for future cycles if your controls offer it. It would not be normal if it is still producing heat after End, tumbles continuously rather than intermittently, or runs with the door open. In those cases, switch it off at the wall and arrange an engineer to check it.

candidates: Moisture-sensing programme extending because the load is still being detected as damp, or the sensor/filter area is dirt (medium)
Programme selector, timer or electronic control fault (medium)
Normal cool-down/anti-crease phase being mistaken for the end of the cycle (low)
plan: The fault they reported is: "won't stop". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
